item.title: Client Says They'll Pay, Nothing Arrives? The Piano Tuner
item.description: The client swears the money is on its way. Day 38, nothing. A quiet story about the piano tuner, the unsent email, and chasing without begging.

item.title: Takings Don't Match Unsold Stock? The Church Hall Key
item.description: Four crates left, a cash box that feels light, and a caretaker jangling keys. A market-stall story about the end-of-day sums that never quite add up.

item.title: Mind Racing at Night? Can't Remember Tomorrow? The Fridge
item.description: 3:20 am, tomorrow's tasks looping in your head, scared you'll forget one. A short story about getting it out of your head and onto one calm page.

item.title: More Edits, Still No Final Payment? The Apple Orchard
item.description: Fourth round of edits, final balance still unpaid. A photographer at a pick-your-own orchard, and what calm looks like when every shoot has a status.

item.title: What to Post for Your Small Business? The Late Pupil
item.description: Staring at your phone, no idea what to post this week? A driving instructor's ten spare minutes, and what a calm content week can feel like.

item.title: ADHD Brain Fog, Can't Plan Your Day? The Cold Kettle
item.description: It's 10:40, the kettle has gone cold twice and you can't pick a first task. A quiet story for freelancers with ADHD brain fog who feel overwhelmed.

item.title: Applied to 100 Jobs, No Reply? The Pub Quiz Tiebreaker
item.description: You've applied to around a hundred jobs and heard almost nothing. A pub quiz tiebreaker, a blank answer, and a calmer way to see where you actually stand.

item.title: Bombed an Interview, Can't Recall What You Said?
item.description: You walked out of the interview and the answers blurred. Here is a calm story about what to do with that sinking feeling, and how to prepare next time.

item.title: Boss Asked If Our API Is Secure? The Dishwasher Silence
item.description: Your boss asks if the API is secure while you stand by the dishwasher, and all you have is 'I think so.' A calm story about a better answer.

item.title: Bank Payments Won't Match Your Invoices? The Paint Mixer
item.description: Three deposits, three vague bank lines, and a paint mixer that takes twelve minutes. A story for freelancers who can't match payments to invoices.

item.title: Client Pays 45 Days Late Every Month? The Shoe Shop Queue
item.description: The money lands on day 45, every month. A freelancer, a card reader in a shoe-shop queue, and a calmer way to deal with a client who's always late.

item.title: Client Pays When Their Client Pays? The Egg Timer
item.description: "I'll pay you once my client pays me." A freelancer's quiet Monday with an egg timer, and a calmer way to answer without begging.

item.title: Client Wants 90 Day Payment Terms? The Bike Rack Call
item.description: The client says their standard is 90 days and you freeze at the bike rack. A calm story for freelancers who worry about long payment terms and chasing money.

item.title: Committed an API Key to GitHub? What Else Did I Miss?
item.description: You pushed an API key to GitHub and fixed it in minutes. The real question is what else you missed. A quiet story from under the salon foils.

item.title: Craft Fair Customer Said Prices Too High? The Oak Board
item.description: A customer sighs at your price tag at the craft fair. Are you underpricing handmade work, or is the number fine? A quiet story about knowing.

item.title: Final Bill Higher Than Your Quote? The Paint Tin Lid
item.description: The customer holds your invoice and says it's higher than the quote. A painter's quiet moment in a finished hallway, and a calmer way to price jobs.

item.title: Customer Wants Extra Work on Your Quote? The Ladder Pause
item.description: You're up the ladder and the customer adds one more job. A quiet story about saying yes to extra work and still getting paid for it, without losing them.

item.title: Everything in Your Head, Can't Delegate? The Pool Lounger
item.description: Day two of a week off and you're still the only one who knows how everything works. A short story about getting it out of your head and letting go.

item.title: Excel Keeps Crashing on a Huge CSV? The Replacement Bus
item.description: The spinner, the 'Not Responding' bar, a call at 9:30. A calm story for anyone whose Excel keeps crashing when they open a huge CSV file.

item.title: External Hard Drive Died, No Backup? The Tuesday Click
item.description: The drive with every client project starts clicking at 8:40 am, and there is no backup. A calm story about what changes once someone else watches your files.

item.title: Forget Deadlines Despite Phone Reminders? The Plum Stall
item.description: Your phone buzzed. You swiped it away. A quiet story for freelancers who forget appointments even with reminders, and what a calmer week can feel like.

item.title: Friend Hasn't Paid Your Invoice? The Opening-Day Latte
item.description: Your friend hired you, loves the work, and still hasn't paid. A quiet story about asking for your money without losing the friendship.

item.title: Double Booked Clients, Tips and Cash Off? The Two Coats
item.description: Two clients at 11:00 and a cash jar that won't match the week. A story for solo stylists who want a calmer chair, calmer books and a calm Sunday.

item.title: No Day Off in Months? Freelancer Burnout and the Voucher
item.description: A balloon voucher expires in three weeks and you can't name one free day. A calm story for freelancers who haven't taken a day off in months.

item.title: How to Politely Fire a Difficult Client: The Green Man
item.description: You've decided to end things with a difficult client, but the email won't write itself. A quiet story about the pause at a red light, and what comes after.

item.title: Made a Mistake on a Client Project? The Car Park Ticket
item.description: You spot your own mistake in a client's files while the car park barrier is stuck. The apology email you can't start, and what it quietly costs you.

item.title: Never Tested Your Backup Restore? The Spare Tyre
item.description: The spare tyre was soft, and your backup restore has never been tried. A calm story about the quiet worry of not knowing whether it would work.

item.title: Overwrote a File, No Backup? The Left-Luggage Counter
item.description: You hit Save over the one file that mattered, and there's no backup. A calm story about that stomach drop, and what a quiet Monday looks like after.

item.title: Should I Stop Working for a Client Who Hasn't Paid?
item.description: The client wants phase two on Monday, but the last invoice is still open. A quiet story about pausing without a fight, and sleeping better.

item.title: Another Contractor Quoted Cheaper? The Bakery Van Text
item.description: The text arrives while you're buying lunch: 'Someone else quoted less.' A story about the quiet panic of a cheaper quote, and what steadies your voice.

item.title: Asked to Review API Security, Don't Know Where to Start?
item.description: A client asks you to review their API security by Friday and your mind goes blank. A quiet story about starting without the knot in your stomach.

item.title: Invoice 'Being Processed' Again? The Art Shop Queue
item.description: Accounts keeps saying your invoice is 'being processed'. A story from an art shop queue about asking calmly, knowing your next step, and finally exhaling.

item.title: Asked to Pick Your Brain for Free? The Ticket Machine
item.description: A 'quick coffee to pick your brain' lands while you feed a parking meter. A calm story about replying warmly, without working for free or losing the lead.

item.title: Client Not Sending Files? The Sauna Bench Question
item.description: The site is due Friday, the shared folder is still empty, and the client has gone quiet. A story for freelancers whose projects stall on someone else's files.

item.title: Refund Request on a Finished Project? The Minigolf Queue
item.description: The client loved the project, then asked for the money back. A calm story about the Saturday you stopped drafting replies in your head and found the words.

item.title: CSV Opens in Excel All in One Column? The Kitchen Table
item.description: The export lands in Excel as one long column and the clock is ticking. A quiet story about messy CSVs, and what a calmer routine feels like.

item.title: Sold Something You Don't Have? The Cricket Tea Hatch
item.description: A Saturday at the cricket club tea hatch, a phone buzz, and an order for a lead you no longer have. A story for makers who sell out by surprise.

item.title: Customer Sent a Security Questionnaire? The Cake Counter
item.description: A customer's security questionnaire about your API lands while you wait for a cake. Half the questions make you freeze. Here's how that moment can feel calmer.

item.title: Excel Numbers Stored as Text Again? The 10 am Report Call
item.description: Your weekly report shows a total of zero because the numbers are text. A short story about a Thursday client call, and a calmer way to start the week.

item.title: Freelance in Germany: Invoices and Hours a Mess? Aisle 7
item.description: Standing in a hardware store when a client asks which hours an invoice covers? A calm story for freelancers in Germany whose invoices and hours are a mess.

item.title: Haven't Posted on LinkedIn in Weeks? The Pottery Stall Ask
item.description: Weeks since your last LinkedIn post, and the guilt arrives at the school pickup line. A quiet story about showing up again without the Sunday panic.

item.title: Job Search Spreadsheet a Mess? The Coach Window Seat
item.description: You meant to follow up last Thursday. Now the spreadsheet is a maze and the reply window may have closed. A quiet story about a calmer job search.

item.title: Asked to Sign Off API Security? The Empty Release Ticket
item.description: Your lead is off tomorrow and the ticket says 'security sign-off: you'. A calm story for the junior developer afraid of missing something.

item.title: Laid Off, Applying Everywhere? The Neighbour's Question
item.description: Laid off and sending applications everywhere? A quiet story about the phone call you can't place, and how to keep track of every application calmly.

item.title: Overstocked, Cash Tied Up in Stock? The Storage Unit
item.description: Rent due Friday, the balance is low, and a storage unit is full of boxes you paid for months ago. A small-business story about cash sitting on shelves.

item.title: Ran Out of Change at Your Market Stall? The Bakery Dash
item.description: A queue at your stall, a 50 note, and a cash box with no change. A calm story for makers who want market days to stop feeling like guesswork.

item.title: Salary Expectations Asked Again? The Mattress Showroom
item.description: A recruiter asks your salary expectations and you can't recall what you told the others. A calm story about keeping one clear record of every job conversation.

item.title: Same Customer Spelled 5 Ways in Excel? The Fair Stand
item.description: Hartmann, Hartman, HARTMANN GmbH: your export counts one client five times. A quiet story about the moment a trade-fair question exposed it.

item.title: Charge a Late Fee to a Client? The Chairlift Question
item.description: Should you charge a late fee when a client pays late? A story about a chairlift, a three-week-old invoice and the awkward feeling of asking.

item.title: SOPs Take Forever to Write? The Picnic Table Phone Call
item.description: Your standard operating procedures stay half-written and your week off isn't one. A short story about the document you keep meaning to finish.
